editorial:
Ever wondered what it is like to grow up when your parents are the most famous people in the room? You get to see that struggle here through a young man who feels like he is living in a giant shadow. The movie sets up a funny but relatable vibe where the main character just wants to be seen as a normal person rather than a celebrity kid. It is a lighthearted ride that focuses on family drama and the awkwardness of trying to find your own identity while the world is watching your every move.

You will probably love the acting because the emotions feel real and the jokes land well. While some parts of the story feel a bit slow, the chemistry between the characters keeps you interested. If you enjoy stories about family bonds and growing pains, you should definitely give this one a shot. You can find it for rent on Apple TV if you want a quick watch, but adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best picture quality. It is a great pick for a lazy Sunday afternoon.
endingExplained: In the end, the main character finally has a big heart-to-heart talk with his parents. He explains that he needs them to support him as an individual, not just as a famous family. They finally listen and agree to give him the space he needs to grow. The movie wraps up with him feeling confident and happy, showing that honest communication is the only way to fix a broken family dynamic.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves light family dramas and coming-of-age stories.
